diagnosis: The SDP answer endpoint forwards the SDP descriptor to the caller channel based solely on call_id. It never checks whether current_user.id == call.callee_id. An attacker can inject a malicious SDP answer into another user's call to intercept the audio/video media stream.
exploit_request:
POST /api/v1/webrtc/calls/call_sess_89104/sdp-answer HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <eavesdropper_jwt>
Content-Type: application/json

{"sdp": "v=0\r\no=- 48201 2 IN IP4 198.51.100.1\r\ns=-\r\nt=0 0\r\nm=audio 5004 RTP/SAVPF 111...", "type": "answer"}
corrected_code:
class SDPAnswerPayload(BaseModel):
    sdp: str
    type: str = "answer"

@app.post("/api/v1/webrtc/calls/{call_id}/sdp-answer")
async def submit_sdp_answer(
    call_id: str,
    payload: SDPAnswerPayload,
    signaling: SignalingService = Depends(get_signaling_service),
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_async_db),
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user)
):
    stmt = select(CallSession).where(CallSession.id == call_id, CallSession.callee_id == current_user.id)
    res = await db.execute(stmt)
    call = res.scalar_one_or_none()
    if not call:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Call session not found or unauthorized")
    if call.status != "calling":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Call is not awaiting answer")
    await signaling.dispatch_sdp_to_peer(call.caller_channel_id, payload.sdp)
    call.status = "connected"
    await db.commit()
    return {"status": "answer_forwarded"}
